_notes: The two orders of E3 round 1 as data. Term lengths, formation stages, and governance are configurable defaults close to real practice and flagged for verification (E3 §18); no engine code tests the key. Real orders and real provinces; every friar, house, and school is generated. Feasts: the order's proper calendar, dates near the Roman and proper calendars and flagged for verification (CLAUDE.md rule 12): the Translation of St. Dominic (24 May), St. Thomas of Villanova (22 September in the order's calendar), and the Augustinian All Saints and dead (13–14 November) especially.

formation.label: Novitiate
formation.line: A brief postulancy folds into the start of the year. Clothing with the habit comes early, and a religious name with it. Then prayer, common life, chant, and the constitutions under the novice master, while the professed of the house watch and decide. At the year's end, a single vow of obedience, understood to hold the others.

formation.label: Studium: philosophy
formation.line: The province's house of studies, and philosophy read the Thomist way. The master of students has you now.

formation.label: Studium: philosophy
formation.line: The second year of philosophy, and the simple vows renewed without ceremony: one long period, the Dominican way. Prior study counts here as it does in a seminary, and counts more for a man who came in with philosophy or theology.

formation.label: Theology I
formation.line: The studium's first real evaluation, and the first part-time ministry outside the house.

formation.label: Theology II
formation.line: What you are for begins to show. The first study dispensations can be asked for now. Simple vows in their final period.

formation.label: Theology III
formation.line: Solemn vows, kneeling before the provincial: the point of no return. Diaconate follows.

formation.label: Theology IV
formation.line: A deacon in a parish, living in community. Ordination, and the first assignment after it.

provinces.name: Province of St. Joseph
provinces.line: The oldest of the four, the eastern seaboard from Maine to Virginia, and the one with the most men in the house of studies.

provinces.name: Province of St. Albert the Great
provinces.line: The middle of the country: campus ministries in college towns, parishes in old industrial cities, and a long memory of the years it was larger.

provinces.name: Province of St. Martin de Porres
provinces.line: The South and Texas, the youngest and the one growing fastest, with more novices than beds some years.

provinces.name: Province of the Most Holy Name of Jesus
provinces.line: The West Coast and the mountains: a school of philosophy and theology, campus parishes, and houses far enough apart that the chapter is the only time the province is in one room.

offices.label: Novice master
offices.line: The men of the next forty years pass through your hands first.

offices.label: Master of students
offices.line: Formation of the student brothers at the house of studies.

offices.label: Regent of studies
offices.line: The intellectual life of the whole province is yours to keep or lose: the studium, the degrees, who is sent to Rome.

offices.label: Promoter of preaching
offices.line: Missions, retreats, and the pulpit across the province.

offices.label: Vocation director
offices.line: Every man who writes to the province writes to you first.

offices.label: Prior
offices.line: The local superior, elected by the house.

offices.label: Prior provincial
offices.line: Elected by the provincial chapter; confirmed by the Master.

credentials.label: Lector of Sacred Theology
credentials.line: The order's own teaching credential, after three years in the classroom.

credentials.label: Master of Sacred Theology
credentials.line: The order's highest academic honour, conferred late for a career of teaching and writing.

houseOffices.label: Procurator
houseOffices.line: The house's books, the bills, and the permissions that cost money. The prior asks you before he says yes to anyone.

houseOffices.label: Sacristan
houseOffices.line: The church, the vestments, the Mass schedule, the candles. The house's liturgy is as good as you keep it.

houseOffices.label: Local promoter of vocations
houseOffices.line: The young men who come to the door, the parish's altar servers, the college down the road. You are the friar they meet first.

houseOffices.label: Guest master
houseOffices.line: Every visitor to the house is yours: the bishop's secretary, the retreatant, the man who wants a bed for a night.

houseOffices.label: Infirmarian
houseOffices.line: The old men and the sick ones: their pills, their doctors, their nights. The house loves the friar who does it well.

houseOffices.label: Librarian
houseOffices.line: The house's books, which are more than it can shelve, and the student brothers who lose them.

houseOffices.label: Cantor
houseOffices.line: The chant. A house that sings the Office well is a house the old men are proud of, and it is your doing or your failure.

houseOffices.label: Assistant to the lay chapter
houseOffices.line: The lay Dominicans who meet in the parlour on the second Tuesday, with a rule older than yours.

apostolates.label: Chaplain at the hospital
apostolates.line: The regional hospital's Catholic chaplaincy: the pager, the intensive care unit, the room where families are told things. The bishop appoints on the provincial's presentation.

apostolates.label: Chaplain at the county jail
apostolates.line: Mass in a gym on Thursdays and a line of men who want to talk. Nobody else in the diocese wants it, which is why it is yours if you ask.

apostolates.label: Teaching at the diocesan seminary
apostolates.line: A course a semester at the diocese's seminary and a seat at its faculty table. The rector asked the provincial for a friar; the bishop signs the appointment.

apostolates.label: Campus ministry at the university
apostolates.line: The nine o'clock Sunday Mass in a lecture hall and the Thursday night that runs late. Vocations come from here, and so does the tiredness.

apostolates.label: Teaching at the diocesan high school
apostolates.line: Four sections of sophomore theology at the diocese's school, where a friar in a habit is a curiosity and then, some years, a vocation.

apostolates.label: The order's school
apostolates.line: A move to one of the province's schools: the classroom, the Friday Mass, the boys.

apostolates.label: A parish of the order
apostolates.line: A move to a parish entrusted to the order, held by two keys: the provincial's and the bishop's.

apostolates.label: The mission
apostolates.line: A move to the province's mission house, a language, and a people who have had the order for fifty years.

apostolates.label: Teaching at the house of studies
apostolates.line: A move to the studium to lecture: the student brothers in your hands, and the road to the province's academic offices.

apostolates.label: Itinerant preaching
apostolates.line: Missions and retreats across the diocese, four nights at a time, from the house you live in. The promoter of preaching puts your name in his book.

apostolates.label: A year of studies at the studium
apostolates.line: Sent to the house of studies to read, not to teach: the lectures, the library, and the licence course if the lector thinks you should. The province sends the men it means to use.

feasts.label: St. Dominic
feasts.line: The founder's day: the province's men who could come, the Mass with the bishop or without him, and a dinner the cook had planned for a month.

feasts.label: St. Thomas Aquinas
feasts.line: The Angelic Doctor's day: a lecture at the studium, a Mass for the students, and the Summa left open on the lectern where someone had been reading it.

feasts.label: St. Catherine of Siena
feasts.line: The Dominican laity filled the front pews for Catherine's day, and the sisters sent flowers and a note that was not entirely about flowers.

feasts.label: Our Lady of the Rosary
feasts.line: The rosary procession went around the block with the confraternity's banner, and the neighbourhood watched from its porches.

feasts.label: St. Martin de Porres
feasts.line: Martin's day: the poor of the neighbourhood fed at the priory door, and the brother who runs the kitchen not to be spoken to before noon.

feasts.label: St. Albert the Great
feasts.line: Albert's day, and a Mass for the scientists among the university's Catholics, three of whom came.

feasts.label: St. Vincent Ferrer
feasts.line: Vincent's day, and a homily on preaching, which the preachers listened to with folded arms.

feasts.label: the Translation of St. Dominic
feasts.line: The Translation kept quietly, a memorial the older men keep and the younger ones look up.

feasts.label: All Saints of the Order
feasts.line: All the saints of the Order, and the litany with more names than anyone in the house could place.

feasts.label: The anniversary of the Order's dead
feasts.line: The dead of the Order were remembered, and the house's own dead read out from the necrology by the youngest professed.

orders.name: Order of St. Augustine
orders.motto: Anima una et cor unum in Deum

formation.label: Pre-novitiate
formation.line: Living in an Augustinian community, working, praying with the friars, beginning studies. Low intensity, high discernment: the community forms its first opinion of you.

formation.label: Novitiate
formation.line: Reception of the habit. A year apart under the novice director: the Rule, the order's history, interiority. At the year's end, first profession of poverty, chastity, and obedience.

formation.label: Theology I
formation.line: A theological union shared with other orders: you live and study beside Franciscans and Servites. Vows are renewed at the year's end, and the community is asked first.

formation.label: Theology II
formation.line: The second year of theology. Renewal again, and the community consulted again.

formation.label: Theology III
formation.line: Solemn profession, the point of no return, after the last of the annual gates.

formation.label: Theology IV
formation.line: Diaconate, and part-time ministry in a parish or a school of the province.

formation.label: Pastoral year
formation.line: A deacon's year in community. Ordination at its end, and the first assignment after it.

priory: Our Mother of Good Counsel Friary
studium: Our Mother of Good Counsel House of Studies

provinces.name: Province of St. Thomas of Villanova
provinces.line: The East Coast, a university at its heart, and the high schools whose alumni love the friars and whose finances do not.

provinces.name: Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel
provinces.line: Chicago and the Midwest, with a thin line of houses reaching down into Texas, a mission abroad, and more retired friars than novices.

provinces.name: Province of St. Augustine
provinces.line: California and the West: a few strong schools, parishes the dioceses would like back, and a novitiate that fills or does not by the year.

offices.label: Novice director
offices.line: A year apart with the novices, and the Rule read aloud.

offices.label: Formation director
offices.line: The student friars at the theological union, and their annual renewals.

offices.label: Vocation director
offices.line: The men who write to the province write to you.

offices.label: School president
offices.line: A budget, a faculty, parents, alumni, and a board: the pastor-equivalent of the education track.

offices.label: Mission superior
offices.line: A long posting abroad, in a church that is not yours.

offices.label: Prior
offices.line: The local superior, elected by the house.

offices.label: Prior provincial
offices.line: Elected by the provincial chapter; confirmed by the Prior General.

credentials.label: Patristics
credentials.line: The order's own patristic institute in Rome: the Fathers, with Augustine at their heart.

credentials.label: Educational administration
credentials.line: The credential the school track runs on.

houseOffices.label: Assistant to the lay fraternity
houseOffices.line: The lay Augustinians who read the Rule on the first Thursday and keep it in kitchens and offices.

houseOffices.label: Prefect of the hall
houseOffices.line: The rota, the noise, and the men who are late for the Office. The house listens to you, which is not the same as liking you.

apostolates.line: The regional hospital's Catholic chaplaincy: the pager, the intensive care unit, the room where families are told things. The bishop appoints on the provincial's presentation.

apostolates.label: Retreat direction
apostolates.line: Weekend retreats for the diocese's parishes and its priests, from the Confessions outward. The bishop's office asks for the friar who can sit with a man.

apostolates.label: A year of studies at the studium
apostolates.line: Sent to the house of studies to read: a year of the lectures and the library, and the order's own writers in the order's own house.

feasts.label: St. Augustine
feasts.line: The father's day: the province's men, the Mass, the Confessions read at table instead of the usual, and the better wine.

feasts.label: St. Monica
feasts.line: Monica's day, and the mothers of the parish at the Mass in numbers, some of them with sons to pray for.

feasts.label: the Conversion of St. Augustine
feasts.line: The Conversion: the garden in Milan read at the Mass, and the novices asked afterwards what it was that Augustine heard.

feasts.label: Our Mother of Good Counsel
feasts.line: Good Counsel's day, with the image garlanded and a novena that ended in it and a crowd that came for the novena and stayed.

feasts.label: St. Rita of Cascia
feasts.line: Rita's day: roses blessed at every Mass, and a line of people with impossible cases and roses to carry home.

feasts.label: St. Nicholas of Tolentino
feasts.line: Nicholas's day: the bread blessed and given out in small bags, and an old woman who takes three, for the sick.

feasts.label: Our Lady of Consolation
feasts.line: Consolation's day, with the cinctures blessed and the confraternity's older members in their places.

feasts.label: St. Thomas of Villanova
feasts.line: The almsgiver's day, and the prior giving away something he would rather have kept, on principle.

feasts.label: All Saints of the Order
feasts.line: All the saints of the Order, and the litany, and the older men supplying the names the younger ones had not learned.

feasts.label: The anniversary of the Order's dead
feasts.line: The dead of the Order remembered at the Mass, and the house's own read out from the necrology.

provinceComplications: A retirement debt the last three chapters voted to study and none voted to pay.
A high school the alumni love and the province cannot afford, and a vote on it coming.
Two parishes the province has held for eighty years that the provincial wants to hand back, and a bishop who has heard.
A novitiate with two novices and a building for forty.
A house of studies the province shares with another province, and a quarrel about whose it is.
A former provincial who has not stopped governing.
A mission abroad that costs more men than the province can send.
A priory the diocese would like back for a parish and the friars will not leave.
A visitation from the general curia announced for next year, and no one sure why.
A generation of friars in their seventies who run everything and a generation in their thirties who wait.
